sourceConceptReview.method: Read Japanese automatic transcript exported from the actual YouTube watch page; concept research only, transcript kept outside the repository.
concepts: Individual differences in response to moving game cameras
Visual motion and stationary body information
Player choice of presentation settings and comfort testing
sourceConceptReview.limitations: Automatic transcript contains errors. Do not copy or translate the original script. Medical explanation and any comfort claims require independent primary-source verification before authoring; do not reuse its medication suggestion as channel advice.

localReview.termScan: Current Korean/English narration and outlines scanned for motion sickness, camera shake, head bob, dizziness and FOV. No current dedicated motion-sickness script found; this alone does not establish a distinct verdict.

fullScriptsRead.comparison: Aspect ratio, monitor size/distance, FOV, target occupancy and UI occlusion teach visibility. They do not teach walking-camera bounce, stable visual reference or player-controlled comfort options. FOV geometry overlaps and must not become a repeated central chapter.
Frame frequency, budgets, deltaTime, frame generation and input latency. Do not repeat the FPS pipeline lecture or promise that a high FPS value cures discomfort.
Character jump speed, gravity, aerial control and anticipation frames. Character movement mechanics differ from camera-motion presentation.
Opening composition directs attention and teaches the first action. Camera guidance and cause/result framing overlap only at the tool level, not the comfort question.

localReview.pickingSidesCurrentWork: Current final script created and reviewed in this turn; camera chapter tracks a spectator's chosen character through framing changes, without comfort or motion-sickness claims.
